(Updates with Bank of America's response in the last paragraph.)

Bank of America (BAC) has launched a sale of investment-grade bonds, Bloomberg reported Friday, citing a person familiar with the matter.

The bank is marketing the bonds in as many as four tranches with maturities ranging from three to 11 years, the report said, adding that the longest-dated tranche is initially being offered at a yield premium of about 1.2 percentage points to Treasuries.

Bloomberg reported that Bank of America was the only one of the six major Wall Street banks that did not tap the high-grade bond market in the third quarter. The bank has raised $17 billion so far in 2026, the least among the group, according to the report.

A Bank of America spokesperson declined to comment to MT Newswires.

title: TFC Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates as Securities Losses, Higher Costs Hurt
detail:
TFC Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates as Securities Losses, Higher Costs Hurt
Zacks Equity Research
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 6:56 AM MST 6 min read
TFC
BAC
JPM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Truist Financial's TFC third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of $1.16 per share rose 11.5% from the prior-year quarter. However, the bottom line missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by a penny.

The reported quarter's results excluded a pre-tax loss of $1.4 billion or 90 cents per share on the sale of available-for-sale securities, along with a pre-tax loan loss reserve recapture of $581 million or 36 cents per share and a pre-tax impact of $106 million or 6 cents per share from the Regional Acceptance Corporation (RAC) loan sale.

Third-quarter 2026 results benefited from higher net interest income (NII), record quarterly wealth management income and higher average deposits. Securities losses and higher non-interest expenses were the undermining factors.

After considering the non-recurring items, net income available to common shareholders was $684 million, or 56 cents per share, compared with $1.35 billion, or $1.04 per share, in the prior-year quarter.

TFC's Revenue Mix Reflects Securities Losses

Total adjusted taxable-equivalent revenues were $5.30 billion, rising 1.3% from the prior-year quarter. GAAP revenues of $3.75 billion declined from $5.19 billion a year ago.

NII was $3.66 billion compared with $3.63 billion in the third quarter of 2025. Taxable-equivalent NII rose 0.7% year over year to $3.71 billion, driven by fixed asset and liability repricing, higher client deposit balances and higher loan balances, partly offset by lower loan spreads and unfavorable deposit mix.

The net interest margin (NIM) contracted 1 basis point year over year to 3.00%.

Non-interest income was $84 million, down substantially from $1.56 billion a year ago, primarily reflecting the securities losses and the RAC loan sale losses. Adjusted non-interest income increased 2.5% to $1.60 billion.

Wealth management income rose 8.8% year over year to $407 million, card and treasury management fees increased 2.1% to $347 million, and lending-related fees grew 16.5% to $120 million. Investment banking (IB) and trading income was $324 million, up 0.3%.

Truist Financial's Cost Trends Show Higher Expenses

Non-interest expenses totaled $3.11 billion, up 3% from $3.01 billion a year ago. This was primarily due to higher personnel expenses, professional fees and outside processing costs. Adjusted non-interest expenses, excluding $40 million of RAC loan sale costs, were $3.07 billion, up 1.7%.

Profitability metrics weakened alongside reported earnings. Return on average common equity was 4.7% and return on average tangible common equity was 7.2% in the quarter compared with 9% and 13.6%, respectively, in the prior-year period.

The efficiency ratio deteriorated to 82.9% from 58.1% in the prior-year quarter.

title: Baird Upgrades Bank of America Stock Despite a Soft Quarter
detail:
Baird Upgrades Bank of America Stock Despite a Soft Quarter
Aditya Raghunath

BAC

Baird Upgrades Bank of America Stock Despite a Soft Quarter ©@PeterPhoto from Getty Images Signature via Canva, @Karola G from Pexels via Canva
Key Stats for Bank of America Stock

Price change for Bank of America stock in last 6 months: -3%

$BAC Stock Price as of Oct. 12: $52

52-Week High: $65

$BAC Stock Price Target: $65

What Happened?

Baird upgraded Bank of America (BAC:NYSE) from Neutral to Outperform on Thursday and set a $62 price target. Baird says the post-earnings sell-off was overdone.

Q3 performance was soft: adjusted EPS of $1.08 missed the $1.10 forecast, and revenue was slightly light. A $1.2 billion regulatory settlement charge cut reported EPS to $0.91.

Weak trading and investment banking also hurt, with Baird reporting adjusted pre-provision net revenue about 5% below expectations.

The core banking business looked healthy, though. Net interest income rose 8% to $16.6 billion. That's the money the bank earns on loans, minus what it pays on deposits.

Net interest yield rose to 2.16%, up 15 basis points from last year, which means the bank is shifting money from low-yielding securities into loans.

BAC Stock Revenue, EBIT and Free Cash Flow Estimates in Billion USD (TIKR)

Loans grew for the tenth quarter in a row. Average loans rose about 6% from last year and deposits reached $2 trillion.

What the Market Is Telling Us About Bank of America Stock

Analysts on the earnings call said the stock opened down about 8%. One said it looked like a confidence problem, made worse by the regulatory settlement.

Management tried to calm those fears. The CFO said the bank has already built the remediation work into its expense base. He also said there is no asset cap, so client business isn't restricted.

Management also gave an upbeat outlook. It expects net interest income growth of about 8% this year. It expects 8% or more in 2027.

It still targets 200 to 300 basis points of positive operating leverage, meaning revenue growing faster than costs.

Baird says Bank of America stock trades near 10 times estimated 2027 earnings, while the current P/E is 11.84.

BAC Stock Valuation Model (TIKR)

Trading revenue was weaker, and the CFO said markets-related interest income could dip in 2027 if rates keep rising.

Still, the bank returned $8.3 billion to shareholders in the quarter. For now, Bank of America stock tells a story of strong core banking offset by a one-time hit.
